pages.title: Benelux
pages.description: politico-economic union between Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg
pages.extract: Benelux  is an economic union comprising three neighbouring monarchies: Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg . The name is formed from the beginning of each country's name. It was a precursor of the European Union.

pages.title: Blaenavon
pages.extract: Blaenavon (Welsh: Blaenafon) is a town in Torfaen, South Wales.  The Blaenavon Industrial Landscape has been named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

pages.title: Central Sulawesi
pages.description: province of Indonesia, on island of Sulawesi
pages.extract: Central Sulawesi (Sulawesi Tengah, abbreviated Sulteng) is the province at the center of the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia.

pages.description: municipality in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil

pages.title: Sakon Nakhon
pages.description: city in Sakon Nakhon province, Thailand

pages.title: Sterling (Virginia)
pages.extract: Sterling is in Loudoun County, Virginia, about 26 miles (42 km) west of Washington, D.C.. The population is approximately 41,000 people (2021).

pages.title: Wartrail and New England
pages.extract: Wartrail and New England are farming communities in the tranquil valleys of the Eastern Cape Drakensberg in the Eastern Cape.  Also known as ‘Wild Mountain Country’ this area offers a safe and relaxing escape in a pristine natural environment

pages.title: Windsor and Eton
pages.description: towns in Windsor and Maidenhead, Berkshire, England
pages.extract:
Windsor and Eton are twin towns, in Berkshire, in the South East of England, separated by the River Thames and joined by Windsor Bridge.

Windsor is an ancient town most famous for its castle, construction of which began in 1075, and which is the largest and oldest occupied castle in the world. The royal standard flies from the keep of the Castle when the King is in residence.
Eton is a smaller town, dominated by Eton College, the ancient public school which educates many of England's establishment, especially those who go on to become politicians, judges and diplomats.

pages.title: Xalapa
pages.description: capital of the Mexican state of Veracruz
pages.extract: Xalapa is the capital of Veracruz in Mexico. Xalapa is a college town that enjoys some fine colonial architecture as well as a nice climate in the highlands above the hot and humid Veracruz coast.

pages.title: Tuguegarao
pages.description: city of the Philippines and capital of the province of Cagayan
pages.extract: Tuguegarao (pronounced as "tu-ge-garao" and commonly shortened as Tugue) is the only city in Cagayan province, and is the transportation hub for the region. It is the regional center of Cagayan Valley, with a reputation for hot weather.

pages.title: Neuwerk
pages.description: Wadden Sea island on the German North Sea coast
pages.extract: Neuwerk is a 3-km² tidal island in the Wadden Sea off the coast of Germany. You can walk around it in an hour. Salt marshes (the "Outland"), lie outside the dikes and provide a hatchery for birds such as oystercatchers, common terns, sandwich terns, black-headed gull, and herring gulls.

pages.title: Masindi
pages.description: place in Western Region of Uganda, Uganda

pages.title: Narromine
pages.description: town in New South Wales, Australia
pages.extract: Narromine is a town in the Central West of New South Wales, around half an hour's drive from Dubbo via A32.

pages.title: Hambantota
pages.description: main town in Hambantota District, Southern Province, Sri Lanka
pages.extract: Hambantota is a town in the Southern Province of Sri Lanka.

pages.title: Remagen
pages.extract: Remagen is a small town in Rhineland Palatinate which was propelled to world fame during World War II when a railway bridge the Wehrmacht had only managed to partially destroy fell into American hands and allowed the Western Allies to cross the Rhine into the German heartland. A famous 1969 film based on the battle titled The Bridge at Remagen ensured the enduring fame of the battle, the bridge and the town.

pages.title: Ingham
pages.extract: Ingham might be a small town of just 4500 (2021) in Far North Queensland, but boasts a rather rich Italian heritage, many of whom migrated to Australia in the 20th century to help out with the region's sugar cane industry. Over half the town's population claims to have some Italian ancestry and draws plenty of visitors from all around the state due to its Australian–Italian Festival.
